Principles: (1) Standard library only - no third-party runtime dependencies; (2) Fail loudly - invalid input produces a clear message and a non-zero exit status or an error response, never a silent wrong answer; (3) Every requirement is testable - each functional requirement maps to at least one automated pytest test; (4) Simplicity - the smallest design that meets the specification; (5) Secure by default - every specification and plan states the security requirements of each feature, following the OWASP Top 10 and the OWASP Application Security Verification Standard, and each one is tested like any other requirement. At minimum: treat every input (arguments, files, archives, network requests and stored data) as untrusted and validate it; never build SQL, shell commands, file paths or markup from untrusted input by string concatenation - use parameterised queries, encode output for the context it is written into, and resolve file paths inside an allowed directory without following links out of it; store passwords only as salted, deliberately slow hashes, and never keep passwords, tokens or other secrets in plaintext; generate identifiers and tokens with a cryptographically secure random generator and compare secrets in constant time; limit the size of every input and the time and memory any input can consume; check access on every operation, including under concurrent requests; create files with the narrowest permissions that work; and never expose personal data or secrets in output, logs or error messages.

## Summary

**Version**: 1.0.0 — initial ratification. The previous file was the unpopulated scaffold with no project-specific values or prior amendments, so there was no earlier governance to supersede and MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH increments don't apply; first concrete adoption is 1.0.0. **Structure** (template hierarchy preserved):

- **I. Standard Library Only** — runtime imports limited to the stdlib; `pytest` allowed as dev-only and barred from runtime code paths.
- **II. Fail Loudly** — clear message naming what was rejected, plus non-zero exit / raise / error response; no bare `except`, no degraded default a caller can't distinguish from a real result.
- **III. Every Requirement Is Testable** — each functional requirement maps to ≥1 `pytest` test, with requirement IDs in test names or docstrings so specification coverage is auditable.
- **IV. Simplicity** — smallest design meeting the spec; explicitly cannot be invoked to drop a security control.
- **V. Secure by Default (NON-NEGOTIABLE)** — every spec states per-feature security requirements against OWASP Top 10 + ASVS, every plan states how they're met, each one tested under Principle III; a spec silent on security doesn't reach planning.
- **Security Baseline** — your minimum controls as eight enforceable clauses (untrusted input, no string-built SQL/shell/paths/markup, credential storage, CSPRNG + constant-time comparison, size/time/memory limits, per-operation access checks under concurrency, narrowest file permissions, output hygiene). Split out of Principle V so the principle stays succinct while the controls remain binding on every feature.
- **Development Workflow & Quality Gates** — spec-first, per-principle Constitution Check in plans, tests gate merges, runtime-dependency gate, reviewer blocking obligations.
- **Governance** — amendment procedure with migration plans, MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH policy, compliance review including the rule that Security Baseline exceptions must be documented with a compensating control.
